subject: Compact SLO follow-up — latency & throughput targets + cost levers
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: Compact SLO follow-up — latency & throughput targets + cost levers

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the product goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard (priority order):
- P95 latency target: 200–300ms for single-turn generative requests ("short responses", ~60 tokens).
- Streaming requirement for multi-turn assistants: first-byte <= 700ms, and steady token emission thereafter.
- Peak concurrency: expected ~450 concurrent users during peak; average concurrency ~90.
- Throughput: sustained ~12 qps with short bursts to ~80 qps.

Cost/performance levers we discussed (rough impact estimates):
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token compute by ~20–40% depending on traffic shape (we'll need sample traces).
- Prefix/KV caching: huge win for repeated context (>40% token reduction when user sessions reuse few tokens).
- Quantization profiles: q4_0 / q8_0 targeted for baseline models; int8 paths for aggressive cost optimization — expect 1.6–2.5x cost reduction vs fp16 at some latency tradeoff.
- Model variants: smaller distilled candidate for short-response paths; heavyweight model for high-quality long-form and fallback.
- Smart routing: split by route (short reply vs. long-form) or by SLA tier.

Attachments: I dropped a compact SLO grid and the traffic sample you shared into the Drive link above. Ben also attached an internal quantization summary (cc'd).

Immediate asks / next steps: 
1) Compact: confirm the P95 SLO (200 vs 300ms) and whether the streaming first-byte goal (700ms) is flexible. If you can confirm by EOD Monday we can size a realistic Dedicated vs Hosted path.
2) Compact: share a 24-hour sample of production request traces (if possible — anonymized) so Ben can run batching/caching sims. Use the Drive folder or reply directly.
3) Redwood: Ben to model cost/latency tradeoffs for three scenarios (Hosted baseline, Dedicated reserved, and Private short-term pilot) — deliverable Thu EOD.
4) Schedule a 45-minute tech deep-dive next week (we have slots Wed/Thu afternoons) — link: https://cal.com/alex_martinez/tech-deep-dive-30

If that aligns, I'll open a mutual action plan in HubSpot and put the tech-deep-dive invite on the calendar.

Thanks — Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95: target is 250ms (we picked 250 as a compromise with the UX team). If hitting 200ms increases cost >30%, we may accept 250ms while we iterate.
- Streaming first-byte: 700ms is a hard preference; anything over 1s will feel laggy to customers.
- Concurrency: the 450 concurrent users is our upper baseline for Q4; there is a chance of short bursts to ~1200 for promotions but those are <15 minutes.

We'll upload a 24-hour anonymized trace to the Drive folder by Monday noon. Also attaching a short doc describing our request shapes (short reply vs. multi-turn assistant).

Can Ben call out what sample format is most useful (we can export request start/first-byte/total latency and token counts).

Looping in a quick ops assessment based on the notes + the sample you dropped in Drive. High-level thoughts: 

1) Batching + scheduling
- Continuous (rolling) batching looks promising given steady baseline qps ~12. For their burst profile we should target an adaptive max-batch of 64 tokens and conservative latency cap to hit ~250ms P95 on smaller requests.

2) Caching
- Prefix caching: if 20–30% of sessions re-use the same prompts we can expect 25–45% token compute reduction. We should instrument an LRU TTL of 30 minutes initially.

3) Quantization paths
- Recommend building two inference paths: q4_0 for most traffic (best latency/cost tradeoff) and int8 for aggressively cost-sensitive routes. q4_0 shows ~1.8x cost reduction vs fp16 in our sims; int8 can go to ~2.3x with a small quality delta in edge cases.

4) Model routing
- Short-reply route: smaller, distilled model (~1B–2B) with q4_0 — keep response quality acceptable for single-turn answers.
- Long-form route: larger 7B+ model (quantized) and fallback to high-precision node only when quality regression is detected.

Deliverables: I'll run sims on their 24h trace when available and produce a 3-scenario cost/latency estimate by Thu EOD (I'll attach quant_profiles_summary.csv).

Ben
